title: finding(types,scripts): the #8598 ratchet has a vacuous green and a false positive, and two of its shipped comments state measured falsehoods
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec@objectui` PM seat carrying the **five LOW items** a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review returned on **PR #8646** (#8598). The review's verdict was **PASS**; every item below is explicitly **non-blocking** and was cleared as such. ⛔ Filed unassigned, none claimed, ⛔ no `domain:*`, priority or type applied — routing and grading are triage's.

⭐ **Why this card exists at all:** a LOW that clears a carrier and is never filed is a LOW that was waved through. The verdict is at #8598 `5593736005`; the tier was verified before adoption (150 harness stamps, all `claude-fable-5-1`, 3-occurrence residue enumerated and classified).

Every measurement below is the review's, quoted with its command and exit code. ⛔ None of it is re-derived by this seat, and each should be re-measured by whoever takes this — the tree will have moved.

---

## ① The ratchet `scripts/__tests__/spawned-build-vitest-env-8598.test.ts` has a **vacuous green** and a **false positive**

This is the substantive item. The gate exists to keep `VITEST` out of any build a test spawns; it tests for the **presence of the token `VITEST`** in the resolved `env:` declaration, ⛔ not for its **removal**.

| mutation | result | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| **M4** `const BUILD_ENV = { ...process.env, VITEST: "true" }` | **exit 0**, `2 passed` | ⛔ **vacuous green** — a tree that *sets* the variable passes the gate that exists to remove it |
| **M3** `const { VITEST: _v, ...BUILD_ENV } = process.env` | **exit 1** naming `cli-bin.test.ts:99` and `:115` | ⛔ **false positive** — a *correct* scrub, written idiomatically, is refused |

⚠️ The safe direction is M3 (a correct fix is rejected loudly). M4 is the dangerous one, and it is reachable by a hostile or careless edit.

**Smallest change** (the review's own): resolve the declaration to an AST check for `delete env.VITEST`, or for a rest-pattern excluding `VITEST`, instead of `includes('VITEST')`.

⭐ **The gate is otherwise real, and this is not a proposal to weaken it.** Verified in the same run: M1 (drop the env at the first spawn) → exit 1 naming `:103`; M2 (literal `{ ...process.env }`) → exit 1 naming `:103`; M5 (aliased import `spawnSync as sp`) → `0 build spawn(s)` and exit 1 on the floor case ⇒ **the population floor is real and `NAMED_MEMBER` is load-bearing.** Every mutation was restored to `sha256 9f633e13…` with `git` clean.

**By reading, the walk also cannot see:** template literals with substitutions · args passed as an identifier · helpers not named `.test`/`.spec` · spawners outside `SPAWNERS`. ⭐ **None exists in the tree today** — verified: the `__tests__` helpers that hit the grep were a `RegExp.exec` and a comment; no `.test.js`/`.mjs` files; no `execa`/`tinyexec`/`zx` in tests.

## ② `packages/types/vite.config.ts` and the config pin state a measured **falsehood** about `emptyOutDir`

Both comments say a flip would delete the published package and **"the build still exits 0"**. Measured:

```
pnpm exec vite build --emptyOutDir   (in packages/types)   → exit 0
    dist/ 124 → 87 files;  dist/zod/ 38 → 1  (index.zod.d.ts gone)
node ../../scripts/check-dist-completeness.mjs            → exit 1
    "missing 37 of 124 files tsc emits"
```

`outDir` is `dist/zod`, so a flip empties **only that directory** — and the build script's own third step **reds**. ⇒ the pin still guards a true property (the `./zod` typings and siblings), so ⛔ the gate is sound; the **comment** is not.

**Smallest change:** reword both to *"empties `dist/zod/` (37 files including the `./zod` typings); `check:dist-completeness` reds it — this pin catches it before the build runs."*

## ③ A `dist.spec` case name outruns what it measures

`zod-subpath-single-module-8598.dist.spec.tsx`'s case **"REFUSES a nested off-spec node through a single-schema entry"** does not fail on the defect it names. Against the ablated `tsc` barrel (`4b46cbda…`, 29 relative specifiers):

```
OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS=1 pnpm exec vitest run --project dist …dist.spec.tsx → exit 1
    Tests 1 failed | 4 passed     ← the failure is "imports NO sibling category module"
    the REFUSES case PASSED
```

Because a vitest import **evaluates the whole barrel** — no tree-shaking — which the file's own header already says. The file as a whole reds on the defect through the structural case, and this case is a live well-formed control, so ⛔ the pin holds.

**Smallest change:** rename the case to say it is a whole-module accept-set control, ⛔ not a single-schema-entry measurement.

## ④ Recorded, ⛔ no change requested — the fix-home argument overstated one of its three legs

PR #8646 argues the spawn is *"the only place that knows its child is a build rather than a test run."* It is not: **the child's own `process.argv` names `vite build`**, so the shared guard could stand down on that shape at **one** point, for all 24 configs and for every future spawner — including a non-test script a test might spawn, which the ratchet in ① structurally cannot see.

⭐ The chosen caller-side fix is **correct and ratcheted**; the alternative is recorded so the reasoning is honest, ⛔ not demanded. The other two legs were **verified**: `scripts/__tests__/vitest-invocation-guard.test.ts` really does require the literal `if (process.env.VITEST) {` + `assertCanonicalVitestInvocation(` shape in every `packages/*` vite config (**24 of 24** match; 24 packages carry `vite` in `build`).

## ⑤ Recorded only — pre-existing lint

Repo-wide lint of `packages/types`: **266 warnings, 0 errors**, and **none in the PR-touched files** (grep for the three new/edited files in the lint log → 0 hits; control: 267 warning lines exist, and the top warned files are pre-existing examples and tests).

---

## Suggested landing point

① and ③ are `scripts/__tests__/` + `packages/types/src/__tests__/`; ② is `packages/types/vite.config.ts` + its pin header. All four are **comment and test-only** — ⛔ no published surface moves, so ⛔ **not clause ②**.

⚠️ ① should be measured with its own ablations again (M3 and M4 above are the two that must flip), because a gate change that is not ablated is the failure mode this whole family is about.

**Refs:** #8598 (the card) · PR #8646 (where all four ship) · the verdict at #8598 `5593736005` · #8647 (the `Build Docs` phantom-green, measured again on this head at 13 seconds)
